content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is consistently negative (especially > -0.5); model resists mean reversion.
- When sentiment turns negative sharply, reduce forecasted decline rate; model often overreacts to sentiment swings.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when recent sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to adjust for 3–5 day momentum decay after sharp moves.
- If sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for risk aversion and policy tightening.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after recent lows unless sentiment is strongly positive (>0.3) and price momentum is accelerating.
